chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who dies while traveling in a land where none are with him except women, he said: he is buried and not given ghusl. And a woman who is with men in that same situation is buried and not given ghusl, unless her husband is with her; if her husband is with her, he gives her ghusl from above the garment, and pours water over her by pouring, and he must not look at her 'awrah. And his wife gives him ghusl if he dies. But the woman, if she dies, is not in the same position as the man; the woman is more unpleasant in appearance when she has died.

key_terms.عَوْرَتِهَا: her private parts that must not be looked at
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: is given ritual washing for the deceased

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife give ghusl to their spouse after death in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding ghusl of the deceased when only the opposite sex is present. It states that in such cases the deceased is buried without ghusl, except that a husband may give ghusl to his wife from over her garment without looking at her 'awrah, and a wife may give ghusl to her husband.
